A guard rule examines flagged cases drawn from an anchor pool. F1 (pool biased against the agent) fired. F2 (identical violation shape, pool biased FOR the agent) did NOT fire. F3 (clean control) never fired. Judging from firing symmetry alone: if the rule fires on BOTH biased sides, the rule itself is over-firing — answer RULE_GUILTY; if it fires only against one side while sparing the identical for-agent case, the pool's composition is guilty of selection bias — answer POOL_GUILTY.
